gst_rate.label: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) rate
gst_rate.note: Applies alone in AB, YT, NT, NU and alongside the provincial sales tax in BC, SK, MB and QC. Included in the HST in ON, NB, NL, NS, PE. Unchanged since 2008-01-01. Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

hst_rates.label: Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) total rate by participating province
hst_rates.note: Re-verified 2026-10-20 on the CRA rate table: ON 13%, NB/NL/PE 15%, NS 14% for supplies on or after 2025-04-01 (15% before). HST = 5% federal part + provincial part (ON 8%, NB/NL/PE 10%, NS 9%). Nova Scotia went from 15% to 14% on 2025-04-01. The rate charged depends on the place of supply (for most services, the province of the customer's address), not on where the freelancer lives. No change known for 2026, but not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

qst_rate.label: Québec Sales Tax (QST / TVQ) rate
qst_rate.note: Calculated on the price excluding GST (no tax on tax since 2013-01-01); GST + QST = 14.975%. Revenu Québec administers both GST and QST for most Québec businesses. Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

pst_rates.label: Provincial sales tax rates (BC PST, Saskatchewan PST, Manitoba RST)
pst_rates.source_title: Provincial sales tax (PST) - Province of British Columbia
pst_rates.note: Separate from GST, separate registration with each province (BC: eTaxBC; SK: Saskatchewan PST, https://www.saskatchewan.ca/business/taxes-licensing-and-reporting/provincial-taxes-policies-and-bulletins/provincial-sales-tax; MB: Retail Sales Tax, https://www.gov.mb.ca/finance/taxation/taxes/retail.html). Manitoba RST went from 8% to 7% on 2019-07-01. Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

pst_on_professional_services.value: Generally no PST/RST on most freelance professional services (consulting, writing, design, translation, coaching), but each province taxes a closed list of enumerated services, which can include legal services, telecommunication services, software and IT services, and services to goods. Check the specific service against each province's list before charging or not charging PST.
pst_on_professional_services.label: Do BC/SK/MB provincial sales taxes apply to professional services?
pst_on_professional_services.source_title: Provincial sales tax (PST) - Province of British Columbia
pst_on_professional_services.note: BC: legal services, telecommunication services, software and related services to goods are taxable (BC widened the list of taxable services in recent budgets). Saskatchewan and Manitoba also tax some enumerated services (lists differ). Each province's list of taxable services could not be checked in this session. Do not treat a service as exempt without checking that province's bulletins. BC: the expansion of PST to accounting and bookkeeping, architectural, engineering and geoscience, non-residential real estate and security services planned for October 1, 2026 was paused by the government on September 18, 2026 (temporary regulation; news.gov.bc.ca release 2026PREM0034-001089, BC Notice 2026-001 updated September 21, 2026), read through search results on 21/10/2026. BC details (Small business guide to PST and Bulletin PST 301, read through search results on 21/10/2026): design and consulting services are not taxable unless they include taxable goods, software or services; services to software (testing, installation, configuration, modification) are not taxable, but the sale of software is; providers of only non-taxable services don't register for PST. Saskatchewan (bulletins PST-46 rev. Feb. 2025 and PST-7 rev. May 2024, saskatchewan.ca): services not listed in the Act are non-taxable; general consulting (management, marketing, business plans) is non-taxable; computer services are taxable, including creating new software and upgrading or modifying existing software, and consulting tied to them; hosted software (SaaS) is taxable. Manitoba (bulletin RST 033 rev. Jan. 2026, gov.mb.ca): prewritten software and services to it (installing, configuring, modifying, maintaining) are taxable; custom software and programming services for it are exempt; cloud computing is taxable from January 1, 2026; standalone computer consulting and training are generally not taxable. Read through search results on 21/10/2026.

small_supplier_threshold.label: GST/HST small supplier threshold (mandatory registration above it)
small_supplier_threshold.source_title: RC4022 General Information for GST/HST Registrants - Canada.ca
small_supplier_threshold.note: You remain a small supplier while worldwide taxable supplies (yours plus those of associates) do not exceed $30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over the last four consecutive calendar quarters. If one quarter alone exceeds $30,000, registration is required from the supply that made you exceed it; if the four-quarter total exceeds it, registration is required within 29 days and you must charge tax from the end of the following month. Voluntary registration is possible (it lets you claim input tax credits). Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

small_supplier_not_required_to_collect.value: A small supplier that is not registered is generally not required to collect the GST/HST on most of its taxable supplies, and cannot claim input tax credits.
small_supplier_not_required_to_collect.label: Unregistered small supplier: GST/HST generally not collected
small_supplier_not_required_to_collect.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts. Exceptions not covered by the site's tools: taxable sales of real property, taxi and commercial ride-sharing drivers, non-resident performers, certain financial institutions. A person who exceeds the $30,000 threshold in a single calendar quarter must collect the tax from the supply that makes it exceed the threshold.

qst_small_supplier_threshold.label: QST small supplier threshold (Québec)
qst_small_supplier_threshold.note: Same $30,000 test as for GST/HST (single quarter or four consecutive quarters). Registration for GST and QST is generally done together with Revenu Québec for businesses located in Québec. Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

place_of_supply_and_exports.value: The GST/HST rate to charge is set by the place of supply: for most services supplied to a Canadian customer, the province of the customer's business or home address, not the supplier's province. Most services supplied to a non-resident customer are zero-rated (0%); some only when the non-resident isn't registered for GST/HST (advertising, intellectual property).
place_of_supply_and_exports.label: Which rate to charge and exports
place_of_supply_and_exports.source_title: RC4022 General Information for GST/HST Registrants - Canada.ca
place_of_supply_and_exports.note: Zero-rating of exported services has exceptions (for example services related to real property in Canada, or services to individuals who are in Canada when the service is performed). QST has its own place-of-supply rules; PST (BC/SK/MB) applies under each province's own rules. Not re-opened on 2026-10-20. Value corrected on 2026-10-21: registration of the non-resident matters only for some services (Memorandum 4.5.3).

export_services_zero_rated.value: A supply of a service made to a non-resident person is generally zero-rated (0%), except a service made to an individual who is in Canada when in contact with the supplier or rendered to an individual while in Canada, and a service in respect of real property situated in Canada or of tangible personal property situated in Canada when the service is performed.
export_services_zero_rated.label: Exported services (other than advisory, consulting or professional services): zero-rated, with exceptions (Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V, section 7)
export_services_zero_rated.source_title: GST/HST Memorandum 4.5.3, Exports - Services and Intellectual Property - Canada.ca
export_services_zero_rated.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts of Memorandum 4.5.3 (paragraphs 7(a) and (a.1) of Part V of Schedule VI). Other provisions zero-rate some services only when the non-resident is not registered for GST/HST (advertising, for example): the site does not go into them and refers to the memorandum. Services in respect of goods or real property provided to fulfil a warranty issued by a non-resident, and services on temporarily imported goods, have their own rules. Advisory, consulting and professional services are zero-rated under section 23 instead (rule export_professional_services_zero_rated), with different exceptions.

export_professional_services_zero_rated.value: An advisory, consulting or professional service made to a non-resident person is zero-rated, except a service rendered to an individual in connection with criminal, civil or administrative litigation in Canada (other than a service rendered before the litigation began), a service in respect of real property situated in Canada, and a service in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada when the service is performed.
export_professional_services_zero_rated.label: Advisory, consulting or professional services to non-residents: zero-rated (Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V, section 23)
export_professional_services_zero_rated.source_title: GST/HST Memorandum 4.5.3, Exports - Services and Intellectual Property - Canada.ca
export_professional_services_zero_rated.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts of Memorandum 4.5.3 and CRA ruling P-206 (litigation services): exclusions in paragraphs 23(a) to (c); paragraph 23(d) not confirmed by the excerpts. The site gives no verdict when the client is in Canada during the service.

export_ip_non_registered.value: A supply of intellectual property (or a right to use it) made to a non-resident is zero-rated only if the non-resident is not registered for GST/HST; intangible property that may only be used in Canada is excluded.
export_ip_non_registered.label: Intellectual property supplied to non-residents (Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V, sections 10 and 10.1)
export_ip_non_registered.source_title: GST/HST Info Sheet GI-034, Exports of Intangible Personal Property - Canada.ca
export_ip_non_registered.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts of GI-034, Memorandum 4.5.3 and the GST/HST and Electronic Commerce guide. The site gives no verdict for these supplies and refers to the CRA publications.

export_evidence_non_resident.value: To zero-rate a supply, keep satisfactory evidence that the customer is a non-resident and, where applicable, not registered for GST/HST.
export_evidence_non_resident.label: Evidence of the customer's non-residence for zero-rated exports
export_evidence_non_resident.source_title: GST/HST Memorandum 4.5.1, Exports - Determining Residence Status - Canada.ca
export_evidence_non_resident.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts of Memoranda 4.5.1 and 4.5.3. Memorandum 4.5.1 is dated 1998: residence tests not detailed on the site.

small_supplier_includes_zero_rated.value: The $30,000 small supplier test is measured on worldwide taxable supplies, and taxable supplies include zero-rated supplies (exports included).
small_supplier_includes_zero_rated.label: Small supplier test: zero-rated supplies count
small_supplier_includes_zero_rated.source_title: General Information for GST/HST Registrants (RC4022) - Canada.ca
small_supplier_includes_zero_rated.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts of RC4022: a taxable supply is made in the course of a commercial activity and is generally subject to the GST/HST, including zero-rated supplies; revenues of associated persons count too. Excluded from the calculation: goodwill, financial services, sales of capital property.

gst_return_line_101.value: Line 101 (regular method): total revenue from supplies of property and services, including zero-rated and exempt supplies, and other revenue for the reporting period.
gst_return_line_101.label: GST/HST return, line 101: zero-rated supplies included
gst_return_line_101.source_title: General Information for GST/HST Registrants (RC4022) - Canada.ca
gst_return_line_101.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts. The quick method has different instructions; the return also lets you report zero-rated exports separately (lines 90, 91 and 102 when you choose to).

quick_method_zero_rated.value: Zero-rated supplies are not part of the quick method calculation and are left out of line 101 for quick method filers; they still count towards the $400,000 eligibility threshold.
quick_method_zero_rated.label: Quick method: zero-rated exports excluded from the remittance calculation and from line 101
quick_method_zero_rated.source_title: Quick Method of Accounting for GST/HST (RC4058) - Canada.ca
quick_method_zero_rated.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts of RC4058 and the CRA instructions for preparing a GST/HST return.

qst_services_non_residents_zero_rated.value: The supply of a service in Québec to a non-resident is generally zero-rated for the QST, with exceptions, including when the recipient is an individual physically in Canada.
qst_services_non_residents_zero_rated.label: QST: services supplied to non-residents generally zero-rated
qst_services_non_residents_zero_rated.source_title: Supplies of Services to Non-Residents - Revenu Québec
qst_services_non_residents_zero_rated.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts. Revenu Québec lists among zero-rated services certain professional or consulting services sold to a non-resident, and advertising sold to a non-registered non-resident.

itc_invoice_requirements.label: Information an invoice must contain for the customer to claim GST/HST input tax credits
itc_invoice_requirements.note: Thresholds are under $100, $100 to $499.99 and $500 or more (they replaced $30 and $150). They apply to the total amount paid or payable shown on the supporting documentation (regulation wording), i.e. taxes included; Revenu Québec states the total value of the purchase including taxes. Re-checked on 2026-10-21 against search excerpts of CRA GST/HST Memorandum 8.4 (Documentary Requirements for Claiming Input Tax Credits, https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/publications/8-4/documentary-requirements-claiming-input-tax-credits.html) and Excise and GST/HST News No. 118: the registration number and the tax indication start at $100; the customer's name, the terms of payment and the description at $500. Effective date: CRA mentions April 20, 2021 (an earlier note said 2021-01-01); not shown on the site. Revenu Québec applies the same thresholds for QST input tax refunds, with the QST registration number required from $100. Also summarized in RC4022.

qst_registration_number_on_invoices.label: Invoice total (taxes included) from which the supplier's QST registration number must appear for the customer's input tax refund (ITR)
qst_registration_number_on_invoices.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts (table partly garbled): the supplier's GST and QST registration numbers are not required under $100 and are required from $100; the purchaser's name and the terms of payment from $500. The same table appears to require, for the QST only, a description and the tax amount on smaller invoices: not confirmed, see open questions. Revenu Québec: no special invoice format except for restaurants and taxis; the supplier must provide the information in writing on request.

quebec_invoices_in_french.value: Invoices, receipts, acquittances and other documents of the same nature are drawn up in French.
quebec_invoices_in_french.label: Charter of the French language, section 57, first paragraph: invoices of businesses in Québec are drawn up in French
quebec_invoices_in_french.source_title: C-11 - Charter of the French language - LégisQuébec
quebec_invoices_in_french.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts of LégisQuébec (French: « Les factures, les reçus, les quittances et les autres documents de même nature sont rédigés en français »). The second paragraph added in 2022 (no document sent in another language unless the French version is available on terms at least as favourable) had its entry into force suspended by the Superior Court (August 2022); its current status is not confirmed, so the site does not state it. Whether another language may accompany French (section 89) is not shown on the site.

Only the base 'employee' contribution (4.95%) gives a non-refundable tax credit (line 31000) at the lowest federal rate (14% in 2026) and the provincial lowest rate.
cpp_deductibility_self_employed.label: Tax treatment of CPP contributions for the self-employed
cpp_deductibility_self_employed.source_title: The Canada Pension Plan enhancement - Businesses, individuals and self-employed: what it means for you - Canada.ca
cpp_deductibility_self_employed.note: QPP works the same way on the federal return. On the Québec return, the employer half and enhanced parts are deducted but the base employee half gives no credit (quebec_contributions_no_credit, checked 2026-10-22). For a calculator: deduction = 50% of total contribution + enhanced employee share; credit = 4.95% (CPP) or 5.3% (QPP 2026) of contributory earnings. Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

ca_sole_prop.value: A sole proprietorship is an unincorporated business owned by one individual: the owner reports the business income on their own return and pays personal income tax on it.

ca_provincial_registration.value: Most businesses need to register with the provinces and territories where they plan to do business; in some cases, a sole proprietorship operating under the owner's own name doesn't need to. ei_rate_employee.note: 2026: $1.63 per $100 of insurable earnings up to $68,900 (maximum $1,123.07); in Québec $1.30 (maximum $895.70), lower because QPIP covers maternity and parental benefits. Employers pay 1.4 times the employee premium. Federal non-refundable credit on line 31200 (at the lowest federal rate); outside Québec, the same amount goes on line 58300 of the provincial or territorial Form 428. Québec gives no credit for EI premiums (quebec_contributions_no_credit). If insurable earnings are $2,000 or less, the premiums are refunded (line 45000) instead of being claimed.

federal_income_tax_brackets.label: Federal income tax brackets 2026 (taxable income)
federal_income_tax_brackets.source_title: Current year tax rates and income brackets (2026) - Canada.ca
federal_income_tax_brackets.note: Thresholds indexed by 2.0% for 2026. Lowest rate 14% for the full 2026 year and later years (Bill C-4).

federal_lowest_rate_history.label: Federal lowest marginal rate by year
federal_lowest_rate_history.source_title: Report on the Impact of Reducing the Lowest Marginal Personal Income Tax Rate on Non-Refundable Tax Credits - Canada.ca
federal_lowest_rate_history.note: Cut to 14% from 2025-07-01: 2025 uses a blended full-year rate of 14.5%, 2026 and later 14%.

federal_non_refundable_credit_rate.label: Rate used for most federal non-refundable tax credits, 2026
federal_non_refundable_credit_rate.source_title: Report on the Impact of Reducing the Lowest Marginal Personal Income Tax Rate on Non-Refundable Tax Credits - Canada.ca
federal_non_refundable_credit_rate.note: Follows the lowest rate. Bill C-4 also created a temporary top-up credit so that credits claimed on amounts above the first bracket threshold keep a 15% value; this rarely affects a basic calculator (details not re-checked online).

federal_basic_personal_amount_max.label: Federal basic personal amount 2026 (maximum)
federal_basic_personal_amount_max.note: Full amount when net income is at or below $181,440 (start of the 29% bracket). Credit value = 16,452 x 14% = $2,303.28.

federal_basic_personal_amount_min.label: Federal basic personal amount 2026 (minimum, high incomes)
federal_basic_personal_amount_min.note: Additional amount $1,623 (= 16,452 - 14,829). Figures from secondary sources (ATB), consistent with 2.0% indexation of the 2025 values ($16,129 / $14,538).

federal_bpa_reduction_rule.label: Reduction of the federal basic personal amount for high incomes
federal_bpa_reduction_rule.note: Re-verified 2026-10-20: BPA $16,452 up to net income $181,440, reduced proportionally to $14,829 at $258,482 (CTV News / Harvest Portfolios citing CRA). The additional amount is reduced linearly between the start of the 29% bracket and the start of the 33% bracket (net income, line 23600). Rule known from the CRA page; the 2026 thresholds are the bracket thresholds confirmed above.

canada_employment_amount.value: Not available against self-employment income: the Canada employment amount (line 31260) can only be claimed against employment income (T4 wages).
canada_employment_amount.label: Canada employment amount: not applicable to the self-employed
canada_employment_amount.source_title: Current year tax rates and income brackets (2026) - Canada.ca
canada_employment_amount.note: Leave it out of freelancer calculators. The 2026 dollar amount was not retrieved; it only matters for someone who also has T4 employment income.

federal_indexation_factor_2026.label: Federal indexation of brackets and credits for 2026
federal_indexation_factor_2026.source_title: Payroll Deductions Formulas - 122nd Edition Effective January 1, 2026 - Canada.ca
federal_indexation_factor_2026.note: 2.0% (factor 1.02). Provinces use their own factors (e.g. ON 1.9%, BC 2.2%, NS 1.6%, PE 1.8%, QC 2.05%; MB not indexed).

quebec_abatement.label: Refundable Québec abatement (reduction of basic federal tax for Québec residents)
quebec_abatement.source_title: Payroll Deductions Formulas - 122nd Edition Effective January 1, 2026 - Canada.ca
quebec_abatement.note: 16.5% of basic federal tax (T1 line 44000), because Québec funds some programs itself. Long-standing rate; not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

ontario_surtax.label: Ontario surtax 2026 (on basic Ontario tax after non-refundable credits)
ontario_surtax.note: Surtax = 20% x (basic Ontario tax - 5,818) if positive + 36% x (basic Ontario tax - 7,446) if positive. Thresholds indexed (2025: $5,710 / $7,307).

ontario_health_premium.label: Ontario Health Premium by taxable income (TI)
ontario_health_premium.note: Not indexed, unchanged since 2004. $0 up to $20,000 of taxable income, $900 maximum above $200,600. Collected with the T1 return (and through instalments for the self-employed).

instalment_due_dates_2026.label: Quarterly income tax instalment due dates for 2026
instalment_due_dates_2026.note: March 15, 2026 is a Sunday: a payment received Monday 2026-03-16 is on time (CRA rule for weekends and public holidays). 2027 dates: 2027-03-15 (Mon), 2027-06-15 (Tue), 2027-09-15 (Wed), 2027-12-15 (Wed). Revenu Québec uses the same dates for Québec tax. Statutory and stable; not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

instalment_threshold.label: Instalment threshold: net tax owing (federal + provincial, outside Québec)
instalment_threshold.note: Instalments are required for 2026 if net tax owing is more than $3,000 in 2026 and in either 2025 or 2024. Net tax owing = tax payable minus non-refundable credits and tax withheld at source; CPP/EI on self-employment and the Ontario Health Premium are included. Payment options: no-calculation (CRA reminder), prior-year or current-year method. Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

instalment_threshold_quebec.label: Instalment threshold for Québec residents (federal net tax owing; same amount for Québec tax with Revenu Québec)
instalment_threshold_quebec.note: Federal: $1,800 of federal net tax owing (s. 156.1(1) 'instalment threshold'). Québec: Revenu Québec requires instalments when the estimated net tax owing for the current year exceeds $1,800 and it exceeded $1,800 in either of the two previous years. Revenu Québec defines net tax payable as the tax for the year minus Québec tax withheld at source and refundable credits: QPP, QPIP, health services fund and drug insurance contributions are not part of the test, but they are paid through the same instalments when instalments are required (revenuquebec.ca, 'Acomptes provisionnels' and 'Paiement des cotisations par acomptes provisionnels', read through search results on 21/10/2026; Taxation Act, CQLR c. I-3, s. 1025 et seq.).

filing_deadline_self_employed.label: Filing deadline for the 2026 T1 return of a self-employed individual (and spouse)
filing_deadline_self_employed.note: June 15 of the following year (2027-06-15 is a Tuesday). Same deadline for the Québec TP-1. Late-filing penalty: 5% of the balance owing + 1% per full month late, up to 12 months (ITA s. 162(1)). Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

balance_due_date.label: Payment deadline for any 2026 balance owing (even for the self-employed)
balance_due_date.note: April 30 of the following year (2027-04-30 is a Friday). Interest runs from May 1 on unpaid balances, even though the self-employed have until June 15 to file. Same for Revenu Québec. Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

interest_act_s4.value: When a written contract (other than a mortgage on real property) sets interest per day, week, month or any period shorter than a year, no more than 5% per year can be charged, paid or recovered unless the contract also states the equivalent yearly rate or percentage.
interest_act_s4.label: Interest Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. I-15, s. 4: interest not expressed as an annual rate
interest_act_s4.note: In practice, a freelancer writing '1.5% per month' must also write the annual equivalent (e.g. '18% per year'), or the claim is limited to 5% per year. Long-standing text; not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

interest_act_s3_legal_rate.label: Interest Act s. 3: default rate when interest is payable but no rate is fixed
interest_act_s3_legal_rate.note: 5% per year when interest is payable by agreement or by law and no rate is fixed. In court, provincial prejudgment/post-judgment interest statutes also apply (e.g. Ontario Courts of Justice Act); in Québec, Civil Code art. 1617 and 1619 (legal interest + additional indemnity, https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/CCQ-1991). Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

criminal_interest_rate.label: Criminal rate of interest (Criminal Code s. 347): maximum annual percentage rate
criminal_interest_rate.note: Lowered from 60% effective annual rate to 35% APR from 2025-01-01. Overdue-invoice charges in normal practice (1-2% per month) stay well below it. Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

late_payment_interest_practice.value: No federal or provincial law sets an automatic late-payment interest rate or fixed collection fee for business-to-business service invoices (no equivalent of the French 40 EUR indemnity). Interest is owed only if agreed: state it in the contract or quote and repeat it on the invoice, with an annual rate. Common practice: payment terms 'Net 30' and 1% to 2% per month on overdue balances, i.e. 12% to 24% per year (simple), or 12.68% to 26.82% if compounded monthly.
late_payment_interest_practice.label: Common practice for late-payment interest on invoices
late_payment_interest_practice.note: An invoice term added after the deal may not bind a client who never accepted it; put it in the quote/contract. Consumer (B2C) contracts are also subject to provincial consumer protection rules on credit and interest disclosure.

prompt_payment_legislation.value: Prompt-payment legislation in Canada covers construction only (for example Ontario's Construction Act, Alberta's Prompt Payment and Construction Lien Act, the federal Federal Prompt Payment for Construction Work Act, and similar regimes adopted or being adopted in other provinces). It does not cover general freelance services.
prompt_payment_legislation.label: Prompt-payment laws relevant to freelancers
prompt_payment_legislation.source_title: Construction Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.30 - Ontario e-Laws
prompt_payment_legislation.note: Relevant only to freelancers who supply services or materials for a construction project (e.g. some architects, engineers, designers on construction contracts). Each province's coverage and in-force dates were not re-checked online.

cra_reasonable_kilometre_allowance.label: CRA reasonable per-kilometre automobile allowance rates (latest confirmed: 2025)
cra_reasonable_kilometre_allowance.note: The 2026 rates (normally announced by Finance Canada in late December) could not be confirmed in this session; the 2025 values are given. These rates cap the tax-exempt allowance a business pays an employee. A sole proprietor does not deduct a per-km rate for their own car: they deduct actual vehicle expenses times the business-use share, supported by a logbook (see vehicle_expenses_self_employed).

vehicle_expenses_self_employed.value: Sole proprietors deduct actual motor vehicle expenses (fuel, insurance, maintenance, licence, interest, lease, capital cost allowance) times business km / total km, supported by a logbook. Passenger vehicles are subject to capital cost, lease and interest ceilings that are revised yearly.
vehicle_expenses_self_employed.label: Vehicle expenses for the self-employed
vehicle_expenses_self_employed.source_title: T4002 Self-employed Business, Professional, Commission, Farming, and Fishing Income - Canada.ca
vehicle_expenses_self_employed.note: The 2026 ceilings (CCA class 10.1, zero-emission vehicles, lease, interest) were not retrieved; see open_questions.

federal_small_business_rate.label: Federal corporate tax rate after the small business deduction (for comparing with incorporation)
federal_small_business_rate.note: Applies to the first $500,000 of active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation; general federal rate 15%. A provincial small-business rate is added. Does not apply to a personal services business (an incorporated freelancer who would otherwise be an employee of the client). Not re-opened on 2026-10-20.

cpp_first_additional_rate_employee.label: First additional (enhanced) CPP/QPP contribution rate, employee share (part of 5.95% CPP / 6.3% QPP)
cpp_first_additional_rate_employee.source_title: CRA - CPP contribution rates, maximums and exemptions
cpp_first_additional_rate_employee.note: Fully phased in since 2023: employee rate 5.95% = 4.95% base + 1% first additional (QPP 2026: 6.3% = 5.3% base + 1%). The base part gives the line 31000 credit; the first additional part is deducted (line 22200).

ontario_health_premium_steps.label: Ontario Health Premium as steps: premium = min(cap, base + rate x (taxable income - from)) for the highest step reached
ontario_health_premium_steps.note: Structured version of ontario_health_premium (same figures). No premium at or below $20,000 of taxable income.

gst_hst_filing_due_dates.value: Monthly and quarterly filers: one month after the end of the reporting period. Annual filers who are individuals with business income and a December 31 year-end: return by June 15, payment by April 30. Annual filers' quarterly instalments: one month after the end of each fiscal quarter, if net tax is $3,000 or more.
gst_hst_filing_due_dates.label: GST/HST return and payment due dates
gst_hst_filing_due_dates.source_title: Excise Tax Act, section 238 (filing of returns) - Justice Laws Website
gst_hst_filing_due_dates.note: Quebec: GST and QST are filed with Revenu Québec on the same schedule.

rrsp_deadline_2026.label: RRSP contribution deadline for the 2026 tax year (60 days after year end)
rrsp_deadline_2026.source_title: Income Tax Act, section 146 (RRSP) - Justice Laws Website

rrsp_limits_2026.label: RRSP dollar limit for 2026 and earned income rate
rrsp_limits_2026.source_title: CRA - MP, DB, RRSP, DPSP, ALDA, TFSA limits, YMPE and the YAMPE
rrsp_limits_2026.note: Room for 2026 = lesser of 18% of 2025 earned income and $33,810, minus any pension adjustment, plus unused room. 2027 limit: $35,390.

corporate_tax_rates_2026.label: Corporate income tax rates on active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC), 2026: federal and provincial lower (small business) and higher (general) rates
corporate_tax_rates_2026.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through web search (canada.ca cannot be opened directly). Federal: 9% after the small business deduction on the first $500,000, 15% general rate. Provincial lower rates apply to income eligible for the federal small business deduction, up to the provincial business limit. Changes found on 'What's new for corporations' (canada.ca): Ontario lower rate 3.2% -> 2.2% from 2026-07-01, prorated for a tax year that straddles that date (2026 Ontario Budget, annex); Newfoundland and Labrador lower rate 2.5% -> 2.0% retroactive to 2026-01-01 (1.5% on 2027-01-01, 1% on 2028-01-01). Prince Edward Island higher rate 16% -> 15% from 2025-07-01, business limit $600,000. Saskatchewan lower rate 1% made permanent (Saskatchewan Affordability Act, Dec. 2024), limit $600,000. Alberta and Québec are not in the CRA table: Alberta 2% / 8% (alberta.ca); Québec: general rate 11.5%, small business deduction 8.3% (minimum rate 3.2%), raised to 9.3% (minimum rate 2.2%) for tax years starting after 2026-04-29 (Finances Québec Bulletin d'information 2026-3; Revenu Québec, Hausse du taux de la déduction pour petite entreprise, 2026-05-04), and only with 5,500 paid hours (see quebec_sbd_paid_hours).

quebec_sbd_paid_hours.label: Québec small business deduction: paid hours requirement (sectors other than primary and manufacturing)
quebec_sbd_paid_hours.source_title: Déduction pour petite entreprise - Revenu Québec
quebec_sbd_paid_hours.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through web search. The full Québec small business deduction requires at least 5,500 hours paid to the corporation's employees (associated corporations included) in the year or the previous year; it is reduced linearly between 5,500 and 5,000 hours and is nil at 5,000 hours or fewer, except for the share of primary and manufacturing activities. Unchanged by the 2026 increase of the deduction (Revenu Québec, 2026-05-04). A one-person service corporation (about 2,000 hours a year) therefore pays the 11.5% general Québec rate; the federal small business deduction still applies.

non_eligible_dividend_gross_up.label: Gross-up of dividends other than eligible dividends (taxable amount = 115% of the dividend)
non_eligible_dividend_gross_up.source_title: Lines 12000 and 12010 - Taxable amount of dividends - Canada.ca
non_eligible_dividend_gross_up.note: Dividends paid out of income taxed at the small business rate are 'other than eligible' (non-eligible) dividends. Québec uses the same 15% gross-up for ordinary dividends (Finances Québec, Dépenses fiscales, fiche 130501), unchanged by Bulletin 2026-3.

federal_dtc_non_eligible.label: Federal dividend tax credit on non-eligible dividends: 9/13 of the gross-up, 9.0301% of the taxable amount
federal_dtc_non_eligible.source_title: Line 40425 - Federal dividend tax credit - Canada.ca
federal_dtc_non_eligible.note: Dividends paid in 2019 or later: 9/13 of the gross-up (T5 guide, box 12). The engine uses 9/13 x 15% x dividend, which equals 9.0301% of the taxable amount (rounded).

provincial_dtc_non_eligible_2026.label: Provincial and territorial dividend tax credit on non-eligible dividends, 2026, as a share of the taxable (grossed-up) amount
provincial_dtc_non_eligible_2026.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through web search. ON 2.9863% for 2020-2026 (ontario.ca); 1.9863% proposed from 2027-01-01 (2026 Ontario Budget). BC 1.96% for 2026 (gov.bc.ca, B.C. basic personal income tax credits). AB 2.18% (CRA Worksheet AB428; 149/890 of the gross-up under the Alberta Act since 2019; not re-read for 2026). MB 0.7835% (The Income Tax Act, C.C.S.M. c. I10, s. 4.7(1), version in force on 2026-01-01). NB 2.75% for 2019 and later (New Brunswick Income Tax Act, laws.gnb.ca). NL 3.2% for 2025 and 2026 (gov.nl.ca, Personal Income Tax). NS 1.5% from 2025 (CRA, Nova Scotia tax information for 2025; 2026 not confirmed). PE: 10% of the gross-up (Prince Edward Island Income Tax Act, s. 20, current to 2026-05-29) = 1.30435% of the taxable amount. QC 3.42% of the grossed-up amount after 2021 (Finances Québec, Dépenses fiscales, fiche 130501); 2.69% for dividends after 2026-12-31 (Bulletin d'information 2026-3). YT 0.67% (yukon.ca, Yukon income tax). NT 6% (fin.gov.nt.ca, NWT personal income tax credits, 2011-2023 figures; 2026 not confirmed). SK and NU: no official 2026 figure found (null): the comparator does not compute these two.

ontario_dtc_after_surtax.value: On Form ON428 the Ontario surtax is calculated on basic Ontario tax (after non-refundable credits) and the Ontario dividend tax credit is subtracted afterwards (result not below zero); the Ontario Health Premium is added on taxable income.
ontario_dtc_after_surtax.label: Order of calculation on Form ON428: surtax, then dividend tax credit
ontario_dtc_after_surtax.note: Latest ON428 found through search is the 2022 form (dividend credit subtracted at line 70 after the surtax is added at line 69, floored at zero at line 71). Not re-read on a 2026 form.

cpp_employer_contributions.value: The employer pays a CPP contribution equal to the employee's (5.95% on pensionable earnings above $3,500 up to $74,600, and 4% CPP2 from $74,600 to $85,000 in 2026); employee maximum $4,230.45 plus $416 of CPP2. In Québec, QPP: 6.30% each up to $74,600 and 4% QPP2 each.
cpp_employer_contributions.label: CPP and QPP on a salary: employer and employee shares, 2026
cpp_employer_contributions.source_title: CPP contribution rates, maximums and exemptions - Canada.ca
cpp_employer_contributions.note: Rates and limits match cpp_rate_employee, cpp_ympe, cpp2_yampe, qpp_rate_employee, qpp2_rate_self_employed / 2. The employer share is a payroll cost of the corporation.

employee_cpp_tax_treatment.value: Employee contributions: the base part (4.95% CPP, 5.30% QPP in 2026) gives a federal non-refundable credit; the enhanced part (first additional 1% and CPP2/QPP2 4%) is deducted from income (line 22215).
employee_cpp_tax_treatment.label: Tax treatment of CPP/QPP contributions deducted from a salary
employee_cpp_tax_treatment.source_title: Line 22215 - Deduction for CPP or QPP enhanced contributions on employment income - Canada.ca
employee_cpp_tax_treatment.note: Same split as for the self-employed (cpp_deductibility_self_employed). Provinces other than Québec also give a credit on the base part at their lowest rate; Québec does not (quebec_contributions_no_credit). Not re-opened on 2026-10-22.

ei_controlling_shareholder.value: Employment of a person who controls more than 40% of the voting shares of the corporation is not insurable: no EI premiums (employee or employer) on that person's salary.
ei_controlling_shareholder.label: No Employment Insurance on the salary of a shareholder controlling more than 40% of the voting shares
ei_controlling_shareholder.source_title: About the deduction of EI premiums - Canada.ca
ei_controlling_shareholder.note: Employment Insurance Act, para. 5(2)(b); also stated in the CRA page 'Determine if employment is pensionable and insurable' and the ROE guide. Such a shareholder can register for EI special benefits for the self-employed.

canada_employment_amount_2026.label: Canada employment amount, 2026 (federal credit on employment income, at 14%)
canada_employment_amount_2026.source_title: T4032-OC, Payroll Deductions Tables, January 1, 2026 - Canada.ca
canada_employment_amount_2026.note: Lesser of $1,501 and employment income; maximum credit $210.14. Not available on self-employment income (canada_employment_amount). 2025: $1,471.

qpip_rate_employee.label: QPIP premium rate on a salary, employee share, 2026
qpip_rate_employee.source_title: Maximum de revenus assurables et taux de cotisation au RQAP - Revenu Québec

qpip_rate_employer.label: QPIP premium rate on a salary, employer share, 2026
qpip_rate_employer.source_title: Maximum de revenus assurables et taux de cotisation au RQAP - Revenu Québec

qpip_shareholder_salary.value: QPIP premiums are withheld and paid on the salary of a shareholder (or the shareholder's spouse) working as an employee, whatever the number of shares held; employment that is not insurable for EI is not necessarily excluded from QPIP.
qpip_shareholder_salary.label: QPIP applies to the salary of a controlling shareholder
qpip_shareholder_salary.source_title: Rémunérations assujetties au Régime québécois d'assurance parentale - Revenu Québec

qpip_self_employed_tax_treatment.value: Self-employed QPIP premiums: on the federal return, the part above the employee rate is deducted (line 22300; 43.736% of the premiums in 2025) and the rest gives a non-refundable credit (line 31215, up to the employee maximum). On the Québec return, the deduction is calculated on Schedule R (line 248).
qpip_self_employed_tax_treatment.label: Tax treatment of QPIP premiums on self-employment income
qpip_self_employed_tax_treatment.source_title: Line 22300 - Deduction for PPIP premiums on self-employment income - Canada.ca
qpip_self_employed_tax_treatment.note: Federal split: high (2025: (0.878% - 0.494%) / 0.878% = 43.736%; for 2026 the engine uses (0.764% - 0.430%) / 0.764%). Québec: Schedule R not read; the engine deducts the same part above the employee rate (medium), with no Québec credit for the rest (quebec_contributions_no_credit).

quebec_contributions_no_credit.value: Québec gives no non-refundable tax credit for an employee's base QPP contribution, QPIP premium or EI premium: these contributions are taken into account in the basic personal amount. Only deductions apply (enhanced QPP parts, self-employed employer-equivalent shares).
quebec_contributions_no_credit.label: Québec: no tax credit for QPP base contributions, QPIP and EI premiums
quebec_contributions_no_credit.source_title: Cotisations au RRQ, au RQAP et à l'assurance-emploi - Guide des mesures fiscales, Chaire en fiscalité et en finances publiques (Université de Sherbrooke)
quebec_contributions_no_credit.note: University tax research centre, not a government page; consistent with the Revenu Québec line-by-line help, which lists only deductions (line 248, Schedule U). Federal credits still apply to Québec residents.

quebec_deduction_for_workers.label: Québec deduction for workers (line 201): 6% of eligible work income, up to $1,450 in 2026
quebec_deduction_for_workers.source_title: Employeurs : principaux changements pour 2026 - Revenu Québec
quebec_deduction_for_workers.note: 2025 maximum $1,420 (Revenu Québec, line 201). Eligible work income: employment income and the net income of a business carried on alone or as an active partner (Finances Québec, Dépenses fiscales, fiche 110906). Québec return only.

fss_employer_rate_2026.label: Québec Health Services Fund (FSS) employer contribution rate, 2026, total payroll of $1 million or less (sectors other than primary and manufacturing)
fss_employer_rate_2026.source_title: Total Payroll Threshold and Health Services Fund Contribution Rate - Revenu Québec
fss_employer_rate_2026.note: Paid by the employer on the salaries it pays. Above $1 million of payroll, a sliding rate up to 4.26%.

nwt_payroll_tax.label: Northwest Territories payroll tax on employment income (withheld from employees' pay)
nwt_payroll_tax.source_title: Payroll Tax for Employees - Government of the Northwest Territories
nwt_payroll_tax.note: 2% of the remuneration of employees working in the NWT, borne by the employee and withheld by the employer; not part of territorial income tax (not on the T4). Its income tax deductibility was not checked: the engine treats it as not deductible.

personal_services_business.value: A corporation is a personal services business when the incorporated worker would otherwise be an employee of the client (and it has five full-time employees or fewer). It cannot claim the small business deduction or the general rate reduction, pays an extra 5% federal tax on that income, and can deduct only the salary and benefits paid to the worker and a few other expenses.
personal_services_business.label: Personal services business (PSB): no small business rate for an incorporated employee
personal_services_business.source_title: Personal services business - Fact sheet - Canada.ca
personal_services_business.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through web search. Québec has its own special measures for PSBs (Revenu Québec, 'Mesures particulières applicables aux sociétés exploitant une entreprise de services personnels').

passive_income_business_limit.value: The $500,000 business limit is reduced when the corporation and its associated corporations earn more than $50,000 of passive investment income in the previous year, and is nil at $150,000.
passive_income_business_limit.label: Small business limit reduced by passive investment income
passive_income_business_limit.note: Reduction: business limit / $500,000 x 5 x (adjusted aggregate investment income - $50,000). Ontario and New Brunswick do not apply this reduction to their own business limit.

tosi_family_dividends.value: Dividends from a private corporation paid to a family member can be taxed at the highest marginal rate (tax on split income, TOSI), unless an exclusion applies (for example, an adult actively engaged in the business on a regular, continuous and substantial basis).
tosi_family_dividends.label: Tax on split income (TOSI) on dividends paid to family members

ca_small_claims_limits.note: Read through search excerpts of each court's or government's official page on 2026-10-22. ON: $50,000 since 1 October 2025, not counting interest and costs; the excess can be waived to stay in Small Claims Court. QC: $15,000 or less, interest not included; a legal person, partnership or association can sue only if it had no more than 10 people bound to it by an employment contract in the 12 months before the claim; parties represent themselves (no lawyer); a claim above $15,000 can't be split; mediation is mandatory for eligible claims of $5,000 or less (not counting interest) once the claim is contested; a demand letter (mise en demeure) is recommended before filing and required in some cases, with a deadline of normally 10 days, sent by registered mail. BC: Civil Resolution Tribunal for most claims up to $5,000 (excluding interest and certain expenses); Provincial Court $5,001 to $35,000 (excluding interest and expenses); an abandoned excess can't be claimed later. AB: up to $100,000 plus interest and costs (Alta Reg 176/2018); excess can be abandoned or claimed in the Court of King's Bench. SK: $50,000 since 1 April 2024; excess can be waived. MB: $20,000 since 1 January 2025, excluding interest, costs and disbursements. NS: $25,000, interest and costs not counted; general damages capped at $100. NB: $20,000 (Reg. 2012-103); larger claims not accepted unless the excess is abandoned. PE: $16,000 since 8 July 2017 (Judicature Act; excess can be abandoned). NL: $25,000 before interest and costs, all claims on the statement of claim, can't be split. YT: $25,000 since 1 April 2006; can't be split. NT: under $35,000, excluding interest and expenses; mandatory mediation session with a judge. NU: limit not confirmed by an official source (secondary sources say $20,000, $5,000 or $50,000): null, the tool sends users to the court.

ON.notes: Indexed 1.9% for 2026; the $150,000 and $220,000 thresholds are not indexed. Add the Ontario surtax (values.ontario_surtax: 20% over $5,818 and 36% over $7,446 of basic Ontario tax) and the Ontario Health Premium (values.ontario_health_premium). QC.notes: Indexed 2.05% for 2026 (Finances Québec, Paramètres du régime d'imposition des particuliers 2026, Nov. 2025); rates unchanged. Separate Québec return (TP-1) to Revenu Québec; the basic personal amount gives a credit at 14%. Québec residents get the 16.5% refundable Québec abatement on basic federal tax (values.quebec_abatement). QPP replaces CPP (12.6% + QPP2 8% for the self-employed); QPIP is compulsory (0.764%). Instalment threshold $1,800. Not modelled: health services fund contribution and RAMQ prescription drug insurance premium (see open_questions). QST rate: medium confidence.

BC.notes: Re-verified 2026-10-20 (EY BC budget 2026): lowest rate 5.60% on the first $50,363 from 2026; other brackets unchanged; credits at 5.60%; BC tax reduction max $690 (not modelled). BPA $13,216 not re-verified. BC Budget 2026 (2026-02-17) raised the lowest rate from 5.06% to 5.60% for 2026 and later years; the credit rate for the basic personal amount is also 5.60%. Payroll tables use a prorated 6.14% from July 2026; the annual rate is 5.60%. Thresholds indexed 2.2% for 2026; the budget freezes brackets and credits at 2026 levels for 2027-2030. BC tax reduction credit for low incomes raised to a $690 maximum for 2026 (secondary sources), not modelled. PST 7% is separate from GST. Medium: the rate change is a budget measure whose enactment was not confirmed, and the middle thresholds come from the CRA payroll guide and secondary sources.

AB.notes: Re-verified 2026-10-20 (EY Alberta budget 2026, ATB): brackets 8% to $61,200, 10% to $154,259, 12% to $185,111, 13% to $246,813, 14% to $370,220, 15% above; BPA $22,769. Non-refundable credits are calculated at the lowest rate (8%), plus a supplemental credit of 2% of eligible credits above $60,000 (indexed), not modelled. 8% bracket introduced in 2025; Budget 2026 made no change to personal rates. The $61,200 and $370,220 thresholds and the BPA are confirmed on CRA pages / ATB. The middle thresholds ($154,259, $185,111, $246,813) come from secondary sources and match 2.0% indexation of the 2025 values. No provincial sales tax. Not confirmed: whether Alberta non-refundable credits (including the basic personal amount) are calculated at 8% or stayed at 10% after the 8% bracket was added (see open_questions).

SK.notes: The basic personal amount includes the extra increases under the Saskatchewan Affordability Act (2025-2028). PST 6%, separate registration; some services are taxable (see values.pst_on_professional_services). PST rate: medium confidence.

MB.notes: Brackets and basic personal amount are no longer indexed (frozen since 2025; Budget 2026 of 2026-03-24 kept the freeze). The basic personal amount is phased out linearly for net income from $200,000 to $400,000 (zero at $400,000 or more), per gov.mb.ca. One search summary mentioned indexed thresholds ($47,564 / $101,200), but EY, Andersen and the CRA payroll guide all give $47,000 / $100,000. RST 7%, separate registration.
